messages:
Ava (PM): quick sync — we need to lock acceptance gates for the Optimize toolkit pilot (batching/caching/quant recs + eval-triggered alerts). Customers (VaultAI, ClearDocs) expect measurable cost wins without quality regression.
Ravi (Eng): +1. We should be explicit about measurable SLOs and the minimum change we’ll accept in quality metrics.
Sophie (ML): Agree. Propose: utility metric (task-specific F1 or BLEU where applicable) with 95th perc. latency budget and <5% relative drop in task metric.
Ava (PM): Suggest launch criteria draft: 1) 10–30% cost reduction in pilot workload (tokens/op) 2) <5% quality delta vs control on eval set 3) end-to-end p50/p95 latency within customer SLA 4) alerts firing on eval regressions in prod preview. Thoughts?
Diego (SRE): Need to add operational gates: error-rate <0.1% increase, fallback path validated, rollout canary at 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback.
Carlos (Solutions): From customer side VaultAI wants quant recommendations that are reversible (able to revert per-tenant) and an audit trail for why a quant profile was chosen. ClearDocs cares about caching TTLs that won’t leak PII.
Maya (ProdOps): For pilot gating we also need onboarding checklist: sample prompt sets, representative traffic traces, expected token distribution, and a contact for emergency rollback.
Ravi (Eng): On implementation: batching + KV prefix caching + per-route quant profiles. Need to define config shape. Quick sketch:```yaml
optimize_policy:
  routes:
    - name: "search-embed"
      batching: {max_batch: 64, target_latency_ms: 120}
      caching: {prefix_cache: true, ttl_secs: 300}
      quant_profile: "int8-dynamic"
      eval_alerts: {enabled: true, metric: "embedding_cosine_drop", threshold: 0.02}
```
Sophie (ML): That eval_alerts example is helpful but we need to be careful: eval-triggered alerts must be tied to stable prompt sets and have clear sampling windows (e.g., rolling 24h, min 500 samples). Also add a signal for drift vs label noise.
Ava (PM): Good call. Let's capture acceptance on the eval side: - canonical eval set per-customer (hand-curated) - alerting thresholds with adjustable sensitivity - min sample counts before alert triage.
Carlos (Solutions): For ClearDocs, TTLs must be configurable per-tenant and we should provide a safe default (no caching for PII-tagged responses). That implies we need runtime metadata tagging.
Diego (SRE): Runtime tagging ok but watch perf impact. We should measure tagging cost in microbenchmarks. Also require that cache eviction is visible in the Console.
Ravi (Eng): Prioritization: which of the four pieces do we ship first? My recommendation: 1) batching primitives + safe defaults (low dev risk), 2) caching with tenant TTLs and tagging, 3) quant recommendation engine (higher risk), 4) eval-triggered alerts (ties into monitoring, medium risk).
Sophie (ML): I’d rank eval-alerts higher because it’s the safety net for quant changes. If quant lands without eval-alerting we risk silent quality regression. Move eval-alerts to #2.
Ava (PM): OK compromise: ship batching core + minimal eval-observability for initial pilot, then expand caching + full eval-alerting, then quant recs (with canary guards). Pilot phases: alpha (internal), beta (VaultAI, ClearDocs), GA.
Maya (ProdOps): For each phase we need explicit exit criteria. Example: alpha -> beta requires data from 3 representative workloads and no critical regressions for 72h under canary traffic.
Carlos (Solutions): Also include customer-facing docs: what behaviors to expect, how to roll back, how to interpret cost/quality charts. VaultAI asked for a 1-page runbook.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window requested for optimize-toolkit-alpha on 1765640000 — confirm if OK.
Diego (SRE): Confirmed OK. We’ll reserve a rollback window and ensure circuit-breaker on model fallback.
Ravi (Eng): Action items: - PR for batching primitives (owner: @Ravi) - caching prototype with TTL/tagging (owner: @Diego + @Ravi) - eval-alerting spec (owner: @Sophie) - quant-rec roadmap doc (owner: @Maya + research)
Ava (PM): Owners noted. Please drop short tickets in the Optimize epic by EOD Friday. Also decide on pilot metrics dashboard — I want p50/p95 latency, tokens/op, cost delta, and quality metric with trend + alert state.
Sophie (ML): I’ll put together the eval set template and threshold guidance (will include sample scripts to run locally).
Carlos (Solutions): I’ll draft the customer runbook and sample tenant config.
Maya (ProdOps): Will schedule kickoff with VaultAI and ClearDocs next week — need sign-off from product + engineering.
Ava (PM): Thanks. Last thing: propose we keep quant recommendations out of the initial beta unless the research prototype shows <1% quality delta in offline sim. Strong preference to gate quant aggressively.
Ravi (Eng): Agreed. We’ll only promote quant if we meet the strict offline criteria and have eval-alerting + canary paths.
Ava (PM): Great. If no objections I’ll update the roadmap doc and circulate updated launch gates. :thumbsup:
Diego (SRE): No objections.
Carlos (Solutions): No objections.
Sophie (ML): No objections.
InfraBot: note: thread archived to project Optimize after 7 days of inactivity.
